notes.front: What is infrastructure as a service (IaaS)?
notes.back: A cloud service type in which you rent the hardware in a cloud datacentre and decide yourself what to do with it.
notes.explanation: It is the most flexible category of cloud services and gives the most control over your resources.
notes.example: Like renting an empty unit on an industrial estate: the landlord keeps the building up, and you fit it out as you like.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Describe Infrastructure as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is platform as a service (PaaS)?
notes.back: A cloud service type between renting datacentre space and buying a finished solution: the provider also runs operating systems, middleware and tools.
notes.explanation: It suits providing a complete development environment without having to maintain the infrastructure behind it.
notes.example: Like renting a fully equipped commercial kitchen: you bring the recipes and ingredients, the owner keeps the ovens working.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Describe Platform as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is software as a service (SaaS)?
notes.back: A cloud service type in which you rent or use a fully developed application.
notes.explanation: From a product point of view it is the most complete cloud service model.
notes.example: Like eating at a restaurant: the meal arrives ready, and all you choose is what to order.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Describe Software as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a lift-and-shift migration?
notes.back: Setting up cloud resources similar to your on-premises datacentre, then moving your workloads onto them.
notes.explanation: The training gives it as a common scenario for infrastructure as a service.
notes.example: Like moving house and arranging every room exactly as it was in the old one.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: According to Azure’s shared responsibility article, what do you manage in IaaS?
notes.back: Virtual machines, operating systems and applications.
notes.explanation: The article gives virtual machines, disk storage and virtual networks as IaaS examples.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Shared responsibility in the cloud, “Shared responsibility in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: IaaS (infrastructure as a service): You manage virtual machines, operating systems, and applications.

notes.front: In IaaS, which three things does the cloud provider look after?
notes.back: The hardware, network connectivity to the internet, and physical security.
notes.explanation: Everything else, from the operating system to storage configuration, is yours.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Describe Infrastructure as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: According to Azure’s shared responsibility article, what do you not have to manage in PaaS?
notes.back: Virtual machines or operating systems: you deploy applications without managing them.
notes.explanation: The article’s PaaS examples include Azure App Service and Azure Storage.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Shared responsibility in the cloud, “Shared responsibility in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: PaaS (platform as a service): You deploy applications without managing VMs or operating systems.

notes.front: In PaaS, what do you focus on while the provider runs the platform?
notes.back: Your application code, your data and your access controls.
notes.explanation: The provider manages the physical infrastructure and platform parts such as operating systems, middleware and managed runtimes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Responsibility focus in PaaS”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In PaaS, you do not have to worry about the {{c1::licensing or patching}} of operating systems and databases.
notes.explanation: The provider maintains the operating systems, middleware, development tools and analytics services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Describe Platform as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In SaaS, what do you still mainly manage?
notes.back: Your data, your identity and access settings, and the access posture of your devices.
notes.explanation: The provider manages almost all of the application stack, including infrastructure, platform and application maintenance.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Responsibility focus in SaaS”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: SaaS has the {{c1::lowest}} operational overhead for customers.
notes.explanation: The provider handles almost all of the application stack, leaving the customer with data, access and devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Responsibility focus in SaaS”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: According to Azure’s shared responsibility article, what does Microsoft manage in PaaS and SaaS under “platform services”?
notes.back: Operating systems, runtime environments and middleware.
notes.explanation: This is part of the underlying infrastructure the article places with Microsoft.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Shared responsibility in the cloud, “Microsoft responsibilities”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Platform services - In PaaS and SaaS, Microsoft manages operating systems, runtime environments, and middleware.

notes.front: Who manages network security in SaaS, according to Azure’s shared responsibility article?
notes.back: Microsoft.
notes.explanation: In IaaS you configure all network security; in PaaS it is shared, with Microsoft providing a baseline.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Shared responsibility in the cloud, “Shared responsibilities explained”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: In IaaS, you configure all network security including firewalls and network segmentation. In PaaS, Microsoft provides baseline network security, but you configure application-level network controls. In SaaS, Microsoft manages network security.

notes.front: In IaaS, who is responsible for deployed applications?
notes.back: You are, fully.
notes.explanation: In PaaS and SaaS, Microsoft manages parts of the application stack, but configuration, code security and access controls stay yours.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Shared responsibility in the cloud, “Shared responsibilities explained”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Applications - In IaaS, you're fully responsible for deployed applications. In PaaS and SaaS, Microsoft manages parts of the application stack, but you're responsible for application configuration, code security, and access controls.

notes.front: Under the shared responsibility model, which service type places the most responsibility on the customer, and which the most on the provider?
notes.back: IaaS places the most on the customer; SaaS places the most on the provider. PaaS sits in between.
notes.explanation: The training describes PaaS as a middle ground that spreads responsibility between the two.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the shared responsibility model, “How responsibilities shift in cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why does IaaS suit testing and development?
notes.back: You can quickly replicate set configurations and start up or shut down environments rapidly, while keeping complete control.
notes.explanation: The training lists testing and development beside lift-and-shift migration as IaaS scenarios.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does PaaS reduce the coding developers must do when used as a development framework?
notes.back: It includes built-in components and cloud features such as scalability, high availability and multitenant capability.
notes.explanation: Developers build on the framework instead of creating those features themselves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two common scenarios for SaaS?
notes.back: Two of: email and messaging; productivity applications; finance and expense tracking.
notes.explanation: All are fully developed applications you simply use.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: IaaS, PaaS or SaaS? A company rents cloud virtual machines, installs its own operating system and configures its own storage.
notes.back: IaaS.
notes.explanation: Installing and maintaining the operating system and configuring storage are your jobs in IaaS.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Describe Infrastructure as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: IaaS, PaaS or SaaS? A school signs up for a hosted email service and only manages its users and their data.
notes.back: SaaS.
notes.explanation: Email is a common SaaS example, and in SaaS you mainly manage data, identities and access.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Describe Software as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A small development team wants to deploy its own web application code and never think about operating system patches. Which service type fits best?
notes.back: C: PaaS.
notes.choices:
A) IaaS
B) SaaS
C) PaaS
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: in IaaS the team would patch the operating system itself. B is wrong: SaaS is a finished application, so there is nowhere to deploy its own code.
notes.explanation: In PaaS the provider maintains the operating systems, and the team focuses on its code and data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Responsibility focus in PaaS”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A retailer wants ready-made tools to mine its sales data for patterns and predict demand, without running the platform itself. Which service type does the training suggest?
notes.back: PaaS, used for analytics or business intelligence.
notes.explanation: PaaS tools let teams analyse and mine data, find patterns and predict outcomes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Platform as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A manufacturer must leave its ageing server room within six months, and wants to rebuild the same set-up in the cloud and move its workloads unchanged. Which service type fits, and what is the move called?
notes.back: IaaS, for a lift-and-shift migration.
notes.explanation: Lift-and-shift means setting up cloud resources like your datacentre and moving workloads onto that IaaS infrastructure.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Infrastructure as a Service, “Scenarios”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: IaaS versus SaaS: which is the most flexible, and which is the easiest to get running?
notes.back: IaaS is the most flexible, with the most control. SaaS is the least flexible but the easiest to get running.
notes.explanation: SaaS needs the least technical knowledge to use fully; PaaS lies between the two.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Software as a Service, “Describe Software as a Service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For security, which service type gives maximum control, and which take care of patches and maintenance for you?
notes.back: IaaS gives maximum control; PaaS and SaaS take care of patches and maintenance automatically.
notes.explanation: In IaaS you manage the operating systems and installed software, including patches and maintenance.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
